data.title: Moody’s to Take Minority Stake in Philippine Rating Firm
data.description: Moody’s Corp. has agreed to acquire a minority stake in Philippine Rating Services Corp. as it seeks to tap debt-market growth in the Philippines and across Southeast Asia, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Binance Wallet Adds Predictdotfun Prediction Markets Integration and Referral Features
data.description: Binance Wallet announced on X that users can now access Prediction Markets features through the @Predictdotfun integration on Binance Wallet. The update also allows users to activate prediction referrals through the Predict dApp, where referrers can earn a 10% commission and referees receive 5% off. The referral program is activated through Predict dApp, then Portfolio, then Referral, and then Activate Referral Program. Binance Wallet also summarized features already available on the platform, including Wallet Referral, which lets users earn up to 80% of friends' trading fees while friends receive 10% to 30% off, and Alpha Points, which can be earned for early airdrops and TGEs. The announcement did not provide additional details beyond the listed features and referral terms.

data.title: Binance Wallet Issues General Notice on Prediction Markets Access and Risk Disclosures
data.description:
Binance Wallet announced on X that its products and services may be restricted in certain regions. The announcement said the campaign and related products are not available to residents of the UAE, UK, EU, US, SG, HK, or other restricted jurisdictions, and that access is limited for users in those regions. It also stated that the notice is a general announcement and does not constitute financial or investment advice. The message added that participation involves significant risk, including the loss of capital.

The announcement also included a disclaimer about Prediction Markets. Binance Wallet said Prediction Markets are not provided by Binance ADGM entities and can only be accessed if a user holds a Binance Wallet. It said Binance Wallet Services are provided by Binance Barbados Limited and are not under the supervision of the Financial Services Regulatory Authority or any other regulatory authority. Binance Wallet also said it does not sponsor, endorse, or guarantee third-party services. In addition, the notice stated that Binance does not act as the counterparty in any investments made through the Prediction Markets feature. The announcement said use of the feature involves significant risk, including financial risk, market volatility, regulatory risk, and third-party risks, and that users may lose part or all of what they have invested.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | PBOC Lifts Yuan Fix for Fifth Straight Day Before Trump-Xi Summit
data.description:
China’s central bank strengthened the yuan’s reference rate for a fifth straight day ahead of President Xi Jinping’s summit with US President Donald Trump later this month, according to Bloomberg.

The move was aimed at offsetting the dollar’s recent gains.

data.title: Miami Marlins Option Jumps to 82% on Polymarket Amid Sharp Volatility
data.description: The win probability for the Miami Marlins option in Polymarket’s Miami Marlins vs. Arizona Diamondbacks market surged from 50% one hour earlier to 82%, according to Catcher Predict monitoring. According to ChainCatcher, the move reflected a 32% swing in the submarket and was accompanied by a note to watch for the impact of breaking news.

data.title: STOCKS | Hong Kong Half-Day Short Selling Reaches HK$18.35 Billion
data.description:
Hong Kong's half-day short selling turnover totaled HK$18.35 billion, accounting for 19.06% of market turnover of HK$96.248 billion, with 795 stocks sold short, according to ETNet.

Tracker Fund of Hong Kong (02800) and Southern Hang Seng TECH ETF (03033) were the most shorted names, with HK$2.156 billion and HK$1.217 billion respectively, representing 11.75% and 6.63% of total short selling. Their short sales accounted for 40.64% and 24.29% of each stock's turnover.

XL2 Southern Hynix (07709) and Hang Seng China Enterprises Index (02828) recorded short sales of HK$991 million and HK$762 million, equal to 5.4% and 4.15% of the total. Their short sales made up 65.79% and 44.74% of each stock's turnover. Tracker Fund of Hong Kong closed at HK$25.50, down HK$0.06 or 0.23%; Southern Hang Seng TECH ETF ended at HK$4.268, up HK$0.032 or 0.76%; XL2 Southern Hynix rose HK$0.36 or 0.97% to HK$37.38; and Hang Seng China Enterprises Index fell HK$0.22 or 0.26% to HK$85.44.

data.title: China Tightens Exit And Entry Rules, Linking Border Control To National Security
data.description: According to Nikkei Asia, a new set of Chinese exit and entry rules took effect Tuesday as Beijing tightened its legal framework for border control and explicitly tied decisions on who can enter and leave the country to national security.

data.title: Kevin Bass Calls for Congressional Probe Into Anthropic's Financial Ties to METR
data.description:
X user Kevin Bass said he audited Anthropic's finances and found what he described as alarming results, prompting him to call on Congress to investigate. According to ChainCatcher, Bass argued that Anthropic has built a regulatory-capture system that cannot be shut down and said its structure creates incentives that make self-termination impossible.

Bass said the cycle begins with METR, which Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei proposed as a third-party evaluator of model risk. He claimed METR is financially dependent on Anthropic's success, pointing to more than $700 million in Anthropic stock growth and saying the stock was placed by Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz into Good Ventures Foundation, which he described as a dominant funder across the Anthropic ecosystem.

Bass said the stock was worth $500 million earlier last year and more than $770 million about 16 months later, and argued METR could not afford to disrupt that growth. He also said the same funding source supports groups promoting AI doom, including the Tarbell Center, which has published in The Verge, Science, and the Los Angeles Times. Bass said METR and similar groups are not independent of Anthropic and cannot provide an independent assessment.

data.title: ASIA MIDDAY MOVES | Hong Kong Tech Climbs as Alibaba, Tencent Rise; Seoul, Taiwan Ease Before Fed, BOJ Meetings
data.description:
According to RTHK, HKET and Reuters, Asian equities were mixed at midday Tuesday as investors braced for likely interest-rate decisions from the U.S. Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan this week, with oil prices and U.S. Treasury yields climbing.

Tokyo's Nikkei 225 recovered earlier losses to trade in positive territory, at 63,664.17, up 171.18 points or 0.27% as of 04:33 UTC. Chip-related names were mixed, with Tokyo Electron little changed and Advantest down 1.38%.

Seoul's KOSPI slipped in continuous trade to 6,658.17, down 26.20 points or 0.39% as of 04:33 UTC, extending Monday's more-than-3% drop. Samsung Electronics edged up 0.10% while SK Hynix added 0.24%.

Hong Kong stocks were narrowly lower at the midday break, with the Hang Seng Index closing the morning at 24,859, down 58 points or about 0.23%; morning main-board turnover topped HK$96.2 billion. Financial and property stocks weakened ahead of the Fed meeting, with HSBC off more than 2% and BOC Hong Kong down close to 3%. The Hang Seng Tech Index bucked the trend, ending the morning up 0.76% at 4,350, as Alibaba rose more than 2% and Tencent gained nearly 3%; AI large-model shares faced selling, with Zhipu and MiniMax down around 5% or more.

Taiwan's TAIEX was softer at 45,681.34, down 181.18 points or 0.40% as of 04:33 UTC, as TSMC rose 0.42% while MediaTek fell 1.43%.

In mainland China, the Shanghai Composite was little changed at the midday break at 3,881.41, down 0.10%, while the Shenzhen Component edged up 0.04% to 13,389.63 and the CSI 300 was flat at 4,479.47.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Europe Seeks SpaceX Rivals as NASA Policy Shifts Trans-Atlantic Ties
data.description:
Europe is moving to build rivals to SpaceX as US President Donald Trump’s NASA reshapes trans-Atlantic space ties, according to Bloomberg.

For the second week in a row, Paris is presenting itself as the center of the space industry.

data.title: STOCKS | FTSE Russell Clients Ask About ESG Index Changes for Big Tech
data.description:
FTSE Russell said clients have asked whether they need to reduce holdings in profitable technology stocks because of the environmental, social, and governance impact of artificial intelligence development goals in the sector. According to Sina Finance, FTSE Russell said it will assess each technology company’s sustainability risks on a case-by-case basis, and Lee Clements said the index provider would gradually adjust weights among different technology companies when necessary to reflect those risks.

Clements, head of sustainable investment research at FTSE Russell, said clients have begun asking whether the climate footprint of hyperscale cloud providers would automatically reduce their weight in sustainable indexes. FTSE Russell did not name any specific companies. About $330 billion in passive funds track FTSE Russell sustainable indexes, and the total assets benchmarked to such indexes may be even larger.

data.title: Global Gold ETF Inflows Hit Record Second-Highest Monthly Level in August
data.description: World Gold Council data showed that global gold ETFs saw net inflows of $18 billion in August, or about RMB 120 billion, the second-largest monthly inflow on record. Holdings rose by 121 tonnes to 4,189 tonnes, a record high, while spot gold briefly touched $4,310 intraday on September 15, 2026. According to Jiemian News, central banks also remained a key source of support: global central banks bought a net 289 tonnes of gold in the second quarter, up 62% year on year, and China's central bank extended its gold purchases for a 22nd straight month, lifting China's gold reserves to 76.73 million ounces at the end of August, up 650,000 ounces from the previous month and the largest monthly increase since October 2023. Goldman Sachs said its forecast for gold to reach $4,900 an ounce by the end of 2026 still has upside, citing continued central bank buying and a rebound in investor demand for gold ETFs.

data.title: Binance Pay Offers Asia-Pacific Travel Discounts and Cashback for Eligible Users
data.description: Binance announced on X that eligible users in the Asia-Pacific region can use Binance Pay to book hotels, flights, eSIM services, and other travel-related services for a chance to receive a 25% discount and up to 250 USDT in cashback. The offer is positioned for holiday travel planning and applies to users who meet the stated conditions. No additional terms, dates, or service details were included in the announcement. The post focused on travel bookings made through Binance Pay and highlighted the potential savings available to qualifying users. The announcement did not provide further information on participating providers, redemption steps, or regional restrictions beyond the Asia-Pacific reference. It also did not include any separate promotional explanation or external links.

data.title: Jaguar Land Rover Holds Substantive Talks With NATO Countries Over Defender Military Variant
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) is in "substantive talks" with NATO countries interested in buying a heavily modified military version of its Defender model. The British automaker is seeking new revenue sources through defense budgets as European countries renew an arms race.

data.title: Apple Reportedly Accepts Samsung's 2027 Q1 Memory Chip Quotes
data.description:
Apple has accepted Samsung Electronics' quoted prices for memory chips in the first quarter of 2027, according to a report from the supply chain. DRAM is priced at nearly $2.0 per Gb and NAND flash at nearly $0.33 per Gb, up 30% to 40% from the third-quarter quotes this year.

According to ChainCatcher, Apple had not responded to a request for comment at the time of publication.

data.title: Bill Winters Reflects On Career Decisions At J.P. Morgan And Standard Chartered
data.description: According to CNBC, Standard Chartered CEO Bill Winters reflected on the career choices that took him from an intended diplomatic path into banking at J.P. Morgan, including a move into the derivatives business despite limited experience. He said that when rare opportunities arise, he believes in taking the less conventional route, which he described as the “reckless path.” Winters also discussed his 26 years at J.P. Morgan, the global financial crisis, being fired by Jamie Dimon, his decision to join the U.K. Independent Commission on Banking, and his later return to mainstream banking to lead the turnaround of Standard Chartered.

data.title: Meta and Instagram Face Class Action Over Crypto Scam Ads
data.description:
Meta and Instagram face a class action lawsuit over crypto scam ads. According to Foresight News, plaintiffs said they clicked crypto investment ads on Facebook and Instagram, were redirected to WhatsApp, and then transferred funds to fake trading platforms before being unable to withdraw.

The complaint targets product design rather than content moderation alone, alleging Meta's ad system targets users interested in crypto and investing. It also claims scammers can pass ad review if they bid high enough.

The lawsuit cites reports and alleged internal materials, saying the platforms display about 15 billion scam ads per day and generate about $700 million in annual "violating revenue." It further alleges the company weighed fines against ad revenue and did not adequately block the ads. The plaintiffs are seeking an injunction, disgorgement, damages, and a jury trial.

data.title: Serenity Says AI Capital Spending Beneficiaries Have Stronger Fundamentals Than Short Bets
data.description:
Serenity said Jim Cramer recently backed short positions in Sandisk (SNDK), DRAM, and SK Hynix-related stocks favored by AI investor Leopold. According to Odaily, Serenity said Leopold’s AI capital spending beneficiaries have more attractive fundamentals, citing Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix as trading at about 2.8 to 3 times forward earnings for fiscal 2027.

Serenity added that Samsung has signed a long-term agreement running through 2031, while SK Hynix has a minimum-price arrangement. Serenity also said Sandisk is expected to reach a 50% free cash flow margin and an 80% gross margin by 2030. Other AI capital spending beneficiaries held by Leopold include Bloom Energy (BE), Intel (INTC), and AMD, which Serenity said could see a “reverse Jim Cramer” move in the medium term because of strong fundamentals.

data.title: Bank of Korea Survey Sees Rate Hike to 3.25% by Year-End
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing a Bloomberg survey, the median estimate showed markets expect the Bank of Korea to raise its policy rate by 25 basis points to 3.25% in the fourth quarter. Markets also expect another 25-basis-point increase in the second quarter of 2027, which would lift the policy rate to 3.50%.

The survey raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 3.4% from 3.3%, and its 2027 GDP growth forecast to 2.5% from 2.3%. It kept 2026 consumer price index inflation unchanged at 2.7% and left 2026 export growth unchanged at 9.2%, while raising 2027 export growth to 4.5% from 3.4%.

Chong Hoon Park of Standard Chartered said the semiconductor boom is continuing to boost household income, consumption, and public finances, supporting faster tightening. He added that inflation expectations remain manageable, while tighter global financial conditions are a constraint. The survey was conducted from September 8 to September 14.
